details:
I am reporting a reproducible system-level memory leak associated with VRChat and Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC).

After multiple rounds of investigation using Windows Performance Recorder, xperf, and kernel call-stack tracing, I have directly confirmed that EasyAntiCheat_EOS.sys creates four ETW tracing sessions associated with persistent committed-memory growth in the Windows system process csrss.exe.

This is no longer based solely on timing correlation. The session-creation call stacks directly identify the EAC kernel driver.

THE PROBLEM

Every time VRChat launches, csrss.exe accumulates approximately 230–280 MB of additional committed memory.

While VRChat is running, memory continues accumulating at approximately 50–70 KB/s.

After VRChat exits, the accumulated committed memory is not released.

On my system, csrss.exe reached approximately 10.5 GB of committed memory, with a historical peak of 23.7 GB.

This is not ordinary VRChat or Unity memory consumption. The allocations occur in a critical Windows system process and consume system-wide commit capacity.

DIRECT KERNEL EVIDENCE

The latest capture recorded the following session-creation call stack:

EasyAntiCheat_EOS.sys

  -> NtTraceControl

  -> EtwpStartTrace

  -> EtwpStartLogger

  -> PsCreateSystemThread

The recording captured four EAC-created ETW sessions.

Timeline relative to recording start:

4.02 seconds:

EasyAntiCheat_EOS.sys loads.

4.14 seconds:

EAC creates a Threat-Intelligence tracing session.

Associated csrss.exe allocation: 0.4 MB.

4.87 seconds:

EAC creates a kernel networking tracing session.

Associated allocation: 3.7 MB.

27.40 seconds:

EAC creates a system-wide context-switch and syscall tracing session.

This session exists for approximately four seconds.

Associated allocation: 190.7 MB.

34.16 seconds:

EAC creates a USB controller tracing session.

This session exists for approximately 20 seconds.

Associated allocation: 29.2 MB.

TOTAL ATTRIBUTION

Total csrss.exe committed-memory growth during this recording: approximately 228 MB.

Memory associated with the four confirmed EAC-created ETW sessions: 224 MB.

This accounts for approximately 98.2% of the observed increase.

The remaining 4 MB could not be conclusively attributed because the relevant allocation stacks were unavailable.

ADDITIONAL EVIDENCE

At the moment each tracing session was created, the corresponding EAC driver thread also allocated a 132 KB memory region inside csrss.exe.

These allocations also contained EasyAntiCheat_EOS.sys in their call stacks.

The repeated ETW buffer-allocation path included:

EtwpLogger

  -> EtwpFlushBufferToRealtime

  -> EtwpRealtimeInjectEtwBuffer

  -> EtwpFindUserBufferSpace

  -> NtAllocateVirtualMemory

Previous investigations identified more than 160,000 individual 64 KB virtual memory regions associated with approximately 10 GB of committed memory.

ALTERNATIVE CAUSES INVESTIGATED

GraphicsPerfSvc and Xbox Game Bar were disabled during the later tests. The problem persisted.

Huorong's sysdiag.sys was not present in the captured session-creation stacks.

SteamVR, Desktop+, OyasumiVR, and VRCX did not create the four relevant tracing sessions.

VRChat's Unity process did not directly create these sessions.

All four relevant session-creation stacks identified EasyAntiCheat_EOS.sys.

However, the possibility of other software interfering with memory cleanup has not been completely eliminated.

WHAT REMAINS UNKNOWN

Although EAC's responsibility for creating the four sessions is confirmed, the exact reason their associated committed memory remains allocated has not been established.

The missing evidence concerns memory release and cleanup.

Possible explanations include incomplete cleanup by EAC, a Windows ETW implementation issue, or an interaction with another kernel component.

I am not claiming to have conclusively identified which component is responsible for the failed release.

REPRODUCTION

1. Restart Windows and record the Commit Size of the user-session csrss.exe.

2. Launch VRChat through Steam.

3. Observe the initial increase in csrss.exe committed memory.

4. Keep VRChat running and monitor the continuing growth.

5. Close VRChat completely.

6. Observe that the previously accumulated committed memory is not reclaimed.

SYSTEM INFORMATION

Windows 10 22H2, build 19045.5608

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090

Steam installation of VRChat

Reproduced in desktop mode

VRChat client build: [To be added]

EAC driver version: [To be added]

REQUEST TO VRCHAT AND EPIC/EAC ENGINEERING

Please investigate why EasyAntiCheat_EOS.sys creates these ETW sessions and why their associated allocations remain committed in csrss.exe after the game exits.

In particular, please examine the lifetime and cleanup of real-time ETW sessions, consumers, and their buffers.

I would also appreciate confirmation of whether this behavior is known and whether specific Windows or EAC versions are affected.

The creation attribution is now supported by direct kernel call stacks, and approximately 98.2% of the measured allocation increase in the latest reproduction has been traced to these four EAC-created sessions.

Please escalate this issue to the relevant EAC kernel engineering team.

I can provide additional diagnostic information or attempt another trace capture if necessary.

Thank you.
title: [Confirmed EAC Activity] EasyAntiCheat_EOS.sys Creates ETW Sessions Causing Persistent csrss.exe Commit Growth
